about.title: Methodology & About
about.intro: This community-driven project helps you compute the VRAM, latency and cost requirements of running open-source LLMs on your own hardware or in the cloud without signing in, entirely in your browser.
about.inf1: Model memory: number of parameters × bytes per quantization (e.g. 70B FP8 ≈ 70 GB).
about.inf2: KV cache: 2 × KV head count × head size × layer count × context length × concurrent users; a fragmentation allowance is added.
about.inf3: Total VRAM: model + KV cache + activations + CUDA/runtime overhead; a multi-GPU communication efficiency factor is applied.
about.inf4: TTFT (first token): prefill FLOP requirement ÷ the GPUs' effective FLOP capacity (compute-bound approach).
about.inf5: TPOT (time per token): (active weights + KV cache bytes) ÷ memory bandwidth (bandwidth-bound approach).
about.inf6: Cost: hourly GPU price × number of cards; cloud comparison uses RunPod / Lambda / Modal prices, while on-prem TCO is computed from electricity, PUE and amortization assumptions.
about.ft1: Total training tokens are derived from the dataset token count × epochs; VRAM needs are estimated per method (QLoRA / LoRA / full).
about.ft2: Training time is computed from the selected GPU's throughput and the framework (e.g. Unsloth) speed multiplier; cost comparison across platforms such as Colab / RunPod is provided.
about.data1: Model architectures (parameters, layers, heads, context length): Hugging Face Hub catalog + a hand-curated list of open-source models.
about.data2: GPU specs: built-in presets based on vendor/provider specifications.
about.data3: Hourly cloud prices: periodically collected from RunPod, Lambda and Modal; see the "last update" time in the results panel.
about.warning: Important: All results are analytical estimates; real performance varies with engine configuration, model, hardware and workload. We recommend benchmarking with your own workload before making production decisions.
about.privacy: Privacy (KVKK): This app requires no sign-in, membership or cookies; no personal data is collected or sent to the server. The scenarios you save are stored only in your browser's local storage (localStorage).

model.selectGuide: When choosing a model: (1) Define your task (coding, Turkish, long RAG, reasoning). (2) Pick a parameter size that fits your VRAM (70B FP8 ≈ 70 GB). (3) MoE models are faster on the same VRAM (fewer active params). (4) Use the 🇹🇷 filter for Turkish and the “Hardware Type” and “Provider” filters for your setup. (5) Balance size vs quality with quantization: GGUF works with llama.cpp/Ollama/MLX, FP16/FP8/AWQ with vLLM/TensorRT/SGLang/TGI.

tips.trainingTime: Estimated total training time on the selected hardware and framework.
tips.ftVram: Total VRAM required during fine-tuning (weights + gradients + optimizer + activations).
tips.localElectricity: Estimated electricity cost of training on local hardware (450W assumption).
tips.unslothSavings: Estimated cost savings from Unsloth accelerated kernels vs standard PyTorch HF.
